title: Frontier AI Models Outperform Published Research on Specific Expert Tasks in GDPx Benchmark

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Leading AI agents are achieving performance levels that exceed published academic and professional research on certain specialized tasks, according to materials science PhDs who helped develop the GDPx benchmark. SemiAnalysis staffer Andrew Megalaa said the collaborators found that frontier models were better than expected, with OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra solving one professional sub-task more effectively than a state-of-the-art published reference, indicating the models are reaching "above superhuman baselines" in specific domains.

The breakthrough results contrast with the GDPx benchmark's general difficulty, which tests models on 206 professional tasks across 11 fields including biology and chip design. While the aggregate scores are low—the top model, Claude Opus 5.5, scored just 12%, followed by Google's Gemini 4 Carbon at 10.9%—the research suggests that frontier intelligence is highly "spiky," excelling in narrow, high-value niches even while failing the majority of complex agency tasks.

selectedTweets.text:
SemiAnalysis staffer Andrew Megalaa says materials science PhD collaborators who helped develop SA's GDPx benchmark was surprised by frontier models' capabilities, and even found they outperformed published state-of-the-art results on some tasks:

"Our collaborators found that the models are much, much better than previously expected. And so they had a moment where they had to sit back and be like, 'This is actually better than a lot of the stuff people are putting out there in papers.'"

"In fact, on one of the problems, Astra solved a subtask of a task better than a state-of-the-art published reference."

"It's very clear that the models are very spiky in these categories. And are reaching above superhuman baselines."

selectedTweets.bestBit: Opus 5.5 wins with 12%, closely followed by Gemini 4 Carbon with 10.9%.
selectedTweets.text:
Super interesting Benchmark. GDPx measures how well AI agents handle 206 challenging tasks across 11 economically valuable fields, including chip design, software engineering, finance, and biology.

But here's the interesting part: Opus 5.5 wins with 12%, closely followed by Gemini 4 Carbon with 10.9%. But while performing just 1.1%  worse, Gemini 4 is about 4x cheaper than Opus 5.5. So cost-performance wise Gemini 4 wins by a lot.
